doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Walter Page on playing bass turnarounds
summary: Budd asks Page how he knows what the pianist will do; Page says you just know.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Walter Page. He had been with the Kansas City people and preceded Count Basie I believe. But he became a friend and he liked me. And I talked with these fellows and I would say “Walter, when you play with you and a piano and a drummer in a trio, and when you play a tune, you come to the end of eight bars, there’s a turnaround they call it to go back and some little fill in. And at the end of a tune you have a little something they called a turnaround.” And I said “you play, what you hear played that particular tune, that particular turnaround, but you don’t know what the piano player may do. He may take a sequence of chords or a chromatic ascension of chords or something.” I said “how do you know what he’s going to do?” He said “well doctor,” he said “you just know he’s going to do the right thing” whatever that meant. He’s dead of course, like most of those fellows.
